pr_title: tpcc: Fix partition statement in tpcc roachtest
pr_body:
After #41216, zone configuration statements on partitions have some more
validation applied to them. This fixes #41028, which didn't have enough
information in the zone configuration statement.

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/41484)
This will only fix the roachtest once https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/41506 lands, so I'll wait for that.

Looks like the bors run perished
bors r=nvanbenschoten
not sure whats going on with trying to merge this. CI is failing repeatedly with "no space left on device" while running make bench, and bors isn't cooperating.
Alright, since bors isnt doing so hot, I'm just going to merge this using the button.

comments:
This indicates that the split failed because the expected descriptor different from the actual one; a replica had been added (as a learner). Maybe this has gotten more frequent with learners, but it shouldn't be a new problem and restore should be more resilient to such failures (perhaps retrying each split until it succeeds; after all, they should because splitting turns into a noop once it succeeds; or accepting that some splits won't happen though  that opens the possibility that due to bitrot none of them will happen).

@dt how did this get handled in the past? My assumption is that this is somehow new behavior triggered by learners.

yeah, AFAIK nothing has changed in RESTORE or how it sends splits. Unlike IMPORT where we pinned some of the blame on _competing_ splits, RESTORE pre-splits non-overlapping chunks and then sends each chunk out for sequential splitting, so we don't _expect_ competing splits. AFAIK, we've never had retry on the split -- the scatter I think we've treated as best-effort and just logged on failure, but the split never failed, that I know of, as long as we've had RESTORE. So it does seem like something in kv has changed here if it is failing now? I missed a lot of the previous debugging of these while I was out but I think @ajwerner dug into it a bit.

Does restore wait for initial upreplication? The split failure here indicates that a fourth replica was being added concurrently with the split. That it was a fourth already smells, I'd be surprised if we wanted to go to five replicas for this range. So *maybe* there is some errant replication happening that happens to get caught by RESTORE's splits. Indepdendently, splits should be more robust, I did most of the work to do that already.

Will take a look at the logs at some point, though it may not happen this week.
